goal: Confirm the frozen Block completion and bottom-type delivery contract without importing adjacent unresolved decisions.
description: Scope: Requirements.md and the O01-Q02..Q05/O05-Q01/P01.11-A decision trace only. Context: the owner has frozen reachable Block fallthrough as unit, incompatible T/unit joins as errors, one strict current-Block yield surface, structural reachability errors, Unit-only consumer typing, and contextual built-in never. Target: keep REQ-BC-001..REQ-BC-007 complete, source-observable, and explicitly bounded away from optional layout, Default, generic Unit/ABI work, and the separately frozen Block-exit protocol delivered by child plans. Design Considerations: requirements describe final behavior rather than implementation phases; every later node must cite the stable labels and expose the typed candidate boundary consumed by the exit child. Design Value: prevents implementation details from silently reopening or extending an owner decision. Constraints & Risks: if an owning child contract changes an interface dependency, update Requirements.md and all mappings before source work; do not duplicate child implementation here.

acceptance_criteria.text: Requirements.md states users, scope, non-goals, constraints, and final acceptance for REQ-BC-001..REQ-BC-007.
Every requirement traces to a frozen decision and makes no choice for the explicitly excluded adjacent clusters.

goal: Verify repository gaps and comparable language/compiler experience for the completion algebra.
description: Scope: Evidence.md plus read-only inspection of Token, Parser, AST, Sema, IR, lowering, codegen, tests, and active docs. Context: the current implementation conflates lexical Block yield with function return, lacks Unit-only consumer typing, delegates reachability to backend termination, and contains undefined/i64/default repair paths. Target: cite exact current symbols, contradictions, open-source compiler patterns, and failure lessons that justify each requirement, including the Rust/Kotlin target-resolution and Java structural-reachability experience. Design Considerations: compare rustc-style bottom/join behavior and LLVM unreachable semantics while keeping Styio's symbol-first surface; distinguish evidence from inference. Design Value: keeps the architecture grounded and exposes migration debt before code changes. Constraints & Risks: external examples inform failure avoidance but never override the frozen Styio contract.

acceptance_criteria.text: Evidence.md cites all current implementation paths that synthesize, infer, lower, or document Block results and never-like divergence.
Primary language/compiler sources document unit, bottom-type joins, never fallback failure, and backend unreachable behavior.

goal: Define positive, negative, IR, tooling, and convergence evidence before implementation.
description: Scope: Validation.md and test/gate discovery only. Context: result semantics can appear correct in parser tests while Sema, nested control flow, IR, codegen, formatter, or docs still disagree. Target: map every REQ-BC label to executable tests, static inspections, generated-artifact gates, and final end-to-end checks. Design Considerations: pair every accepted behavior with adjacent rejection coverage and require source spans/diagnostic codes; cover nested Blocks and optimizer behavior. Design Value: prevents a shallow parser-only implementation from being declared complete. Constraints & Risks: commands must name existing gate families or explicitly identify tests to add; no criterion may rely only on prose review.

acceptance_criteria.text: Validation.md maps every REQ-BC label to at least one real executable or static check.

The matrix covers nested Blocks, both yield spellings, explicit Unit yield, Unit-only consumers, structural reachability, incompatible joins, divergence, tokenizer behavior, diagnostics, IR verification, codegen, docs, and removal of obsolete tests.

goal: Freeze the linear completion-summary, AST, IR, and module-boundary architecture.
description: Scope: Architecture.md and interface/scaffold decisions; no feature behavior is claimed complete. Context: ReturnAST, recursive tail inspection, SGReturn, and default backend values currently collapse distinct lexical and function boundaries. Target: define canonical Unit/Never identities, a memoized O(nodes+edges) BlockSummary join algebra, one BlockYieldAST for both spellings, explicit BlockConsumer value/Unit-only typing, structural reachability, a distinct IR Block-result/candidate form, and an outer function adapter that the Block-exit child can consume. Design Considerations: use an algebraic flow summary and verifier boundary; keep AST syntax-only, Sema authoritative, dependencies one-way, and parsing pattern-free. Design Value: one completion data model removes repeated scans, prevents value discard, and prevents backend repair. Constraints & Risks: do not choose optional, generic-Unit, task, cleanup scheduling, fixed failure storage, or public ABI representation here; update architecture first if implementation needs a new cross-module interface.

acceptance_criteria.text: Architecture.md defines module ownership, dependency direction, interfaces, patterns, file ownership, and the total completion join law.
The architecture separates lexical Block yield from function return and explains why each new abstraction earns its complexity.

goal: Converge contextual Unit/Never typing and lexical Block-yield parsing/AST.
description: Scope: src/StyioToken/Token.hpp, src/StyioAST/AST*.hpp, src/StyioParser/*, and parser/tokenizer tests. Context: identifiers already tokenize as NAME, but Unit/Never lack canonical type alternatives and both yield spellings currently create ReturnAST. Target: add canonical contextual type identities, keep never as NAME, parse all frozen direct-body forms, replace ReturnAST with one BlockYieldAST in a complete migration, require inline |;, accept <| (), and attach every yield to its immediate lexical Block structure. Design Considerations: reuse the existing type-name path and parser authority; inline punctuation creates no semantic variant; no keyword table, alternate parser route, AST alias, or compatibility visitor. Design Value: establishes an unambiguous frontend contract for linear Sema analysis. Constraints & Risks: do not implement a never value, general tail expressions, optional layout, or cross-Block return behavior; update all frontend-owned tests atomically.

acceptance_criteria.text: Tokenizer tests prove never remains NAME, and type parser tests accept contextual unit/never without new keyword tokens.
All parser/AST visitors use BlockYieldAST; ReturnAST compatibility code and frontend tests are removed.
Parser tests prove <| expr and |<| expr |; produce the same BlockYieldAST/current-Block owner, require inline |;, accept <| (), and preserve nested lexical ownership.

goal: Implement one memoized Sema completion analysis and deterministic Block-result joins.
description: Scope: src/StyioSema/* and function/control-flow semantic tests. Context: current inference recursively inspects selected tails, treats empty Blocks as undefined, defaults some missing results to i64, and has no Unit-only consumer contract. Target: compute one cached BlockSummary per lexical Block, add reachable fallthrough as unit, join compatible normal exits, drop only proven never edges, type-check each yield against a ValueExpected or UnitOnly consumer, and issue source-located diagnostics for incompatible exits, missing non-unit results, invalid never construction/defaulting, structural unreachability, and Unit-only value loss. Design Considerations: use a compact exit set plus origin spans in one O(nodes+edges) traversal; canonical TypeId equality precedes joins; diagnose a region as unreachable only when every structural incoming edge has completed; no repeated subtree scans or backend repair. Design Value: makes all consumers share one proof of result type and divergence. Constraints & Risks: loops are never only when non-completion is proven; unknown control flow remains reachable/fail-closed, and no optional/default/effect rule is invented.

acceptance_criteria.text: Sema tests prove unit fallthrough, compatible joins, join(T, never)=T, lexical nested yields, and the three direct function-body forms.

Negative tests prove T/unit rejection, missing non-unit result rejection, invalid never values/defaults, Unit-only <| T rejection, and structural same-Block unreachable diagnostics with stable codes/spans independent of optimization.
Static inspection and instrumentation prove one memoized linear completion analysis replaces recursive tail/default inference for this contract.

goal: Lower Sema-proven Block results through StyioIR and LLVM without fabricated values.
description: Scope: src/StyioIR/*, src/StyioLowering/*, src/StyioCodeGen/*, IR verifier tests, pipeline goldens, and security tests. Context: SGReturn currently represents both lexical and function completion, empty SGBlock returns i64 zero, and failed return coercion can use a default runtime value. Target: add one distinct verified Block-result/candidate IR boundary shared by both yield spellings, adapt only the outer function body to SGReturn, emit no payload for unit/never, form PHI/control-flow joins only for compatible values, reject any Unit-only value-discard route, and emit unreachable only for Sema-proven divergence. Design Considerations: verifier failures stop before codegen; no default repair or inline-yield discriminator is allowed on Block/function-result paths; keep generic/ABI and exit-settlement representations out of scope while exposing the typed interface the child consumes. Design Value: backend structure becomes a consumer of semantic proof instead of a second inference engine. Constraints & Risks: preserve existing cleanup/resource behavior until the child performs its one-shot migration; do not partially implement a second epilogue authority in this parent.

acceptance_criteria.text: IR verifier tests reject malformed Block-result joins and Unit-only value discard, distinguish lexical Block completion from SGReturn, and prove both source spellings share one IR form.
Pipeline goldens prove unit/never produce no fabricated integer payload and compatible value joins lower correctly.
Code inspection proves failed Block/function result coercion cannot call a default-return repair path.

goal: Converge active language docs, tooling mirrors, diagnostics, and fixtures on the delivered contract.
description: Scope: Styio Language Design, EBNF, Symbol Reference, ACTIVE-SYNTAX, syntax convergence matrix, frontend/sema/test/docs runbooks, tree-sitter/editor/formatter mirrors, and affected fixtures. Context: active docs and tests still include cross-function wording for nested <| and have no complete Unit/Never join contract. Target: publish one canonical explanation and example set, update tooling to the final AST/type facts, migrate positive fixtures, delete obsolete executable expectations after stable diagnostics are covered, and link the child plans that own adjacent frozen representation/exit contracts. Design Considerations: language SSOT owns semantics; tooling mirrors syntax; indexes/gates are regenerated rather than hand-diverged. Design Value: prevents the old behavior from surviving as documentation or acceptance debt. Constraints & Risks: do not duplicate child Unit/ABI/exit protocol details or document still-open optional/default/effect syntax answers, and do not preserve old behavior under legacy/compat labels.

acceptance_criteria.text: All active SSOT and tooling mirrors state the same lexical Block, dual-spelling normalization, mandatory inline terminator, explicit Unit yield, Unit-only consumer, structural reachability, unit, never, and join rules.
Obsolete cross-Block return fixtures/tests are migrated or removed, with only current negative diagnostics retained.
Syntax convergence, docs index, docs audit, docs lifecycle, and local-information gates pass.

goal: Prove the complete Block completion and bottom-type contract on one head commit.
description: Scope: execution and evidence recording for every Validation.md mapping; source changes only route back to the owning implementation node. Context: frontend, Sema, IR, backend, docs, and tooling can each pass locally while disagreeing end to end. Target: run all standing and REQ-specific checks on one commit, classify every obsolete ReturnAST/cross-Block-return match, record evidence per REQ-BC label, and synchronize Better Plan state. Design Considerations: validate source behavior, diagnostics, IR structure, runtime output, tooling, and generated docs together. Design Value: turns the owner decision into auditable delivery evidence rather than a documentation-only claim. Constraints & Risks: acceptance targets may not be weakened to accommodate implementation; any unresolved adjacent policy remains out of scope and fail-closed.
